entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
entries.description: FDA today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or a high-risk transient ischemic attack.
entries.summary: FDA approves first factor XIa inhibitor, asundexian, for stroke prevention in high‑risk adults.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should note the new indication and consider labeling, interactions with antiplatelet therapy, and potential changes to product dossiers.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherap
entries.summary: FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that has progressed after platinum‑based therapy.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must update product dossiers, labeling, and inform stakeholders about the new indication to ensure compliance and support future regulatory submissions.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Phased implementation of ICH M11: Clinical electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP) – Notice to stakeholders
entries.description: This new guideline provides comprehensive clinical protocol organization with standardized content, with a Template which presents the format and structure of the protocol, including the table of contents, common headers, and contents; and a Technical Specification which presents the conformance, cardinality, and other technical attributes that enable the interoperable electronic exchange of protocol content.
entries.summary: ICH M11 CeSHarP introduces a standardized protocol template and technical specification for interoperable electronic protocol content.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across all therapeutic areas must adopt the new template and technical specifications to ensure compliant protocol submission and interoperability.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice to stakeholders on implementing ICH M13B: Bioequivalence for immediate release solid oral dosage forms: Additional strengths biowaiver
entries.description: Part of the foreseen ICH M13 Guideline series (M13A-C), the ICH M13B Guideline is intended to provide recommendations on obtaining waivers of bioequivalence (BE) studies for one or more additional strengths of a drug product in an application where in vivo BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths. This guideline is applicable to both development and post approval phases for orally administered immediate-release (IR) solid oral dosage forms designed to deliver drugs to the systemic circulation, such as tablets, capsules, and granules/powders for oral suspension. The ICH M13B Guideline is the second Guideline in the foreseen series to describe the scientific and technical aspects of demonstrating BE for additional strengths of a drug product, i.e., obtaining waiver(s) for one or more strengths in an application with multiple strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths following ICH M13A. How regulatory decisions may be made based on BE assessment is out of the scope of this guideline.
entries.summary: Regulators now provide guidance for biowaivers for additional strengths of immediate‑release solid oral dosage forms.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling IR solid oral dosage forms must consider biowaiver options for additional strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one strength.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: ICH guidelines implemented by Health Canada
entries.description: Health Canada has implemented and launched public consultations on several International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, reflecting Canada’s ongoing commitment to global regulatory harmonization. Stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines for consultation by the respective deadlines, as Health Canada will forward all comments to the ICH for consideration in the finalization process. Health Canada has begun implementing finalized guidelines. Stakeholders are encouraged to integrate these guidelines into their drug registration processes.
entries.summary: Health Canada launched public consultations on several ICH guidelines and is implementing finalized guidelines.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review the draft ICH guidelines, provide feedback before the consultation deadline, and integrate the finalized guidelines into their drug registration processes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice for Calquence (302879)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada granted a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Calquence, requiring the sponsor to conduct additional studies to confirm clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs must coordinate the mandated studies and ensure compliance with the conditions to maintain market authorization.

entries.summary: FDA issues final guidance for CGT manufacturers to establish a science‑ and risk‑based potency plan.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams for cell and gene therapies must incorporate these new potency standards into their quality systems and documentation.

entries.description: How to avoid delays when submitting clinical trial application assessments The UK's new clinical trial regulations came into force on 28 April 2026, introducing a more flexible and risk-proportionate approach to clinical trial assessment. Sponsors now submit a single clinical …

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
entries.description: FDA today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis.
entries.summary: The FDA has approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection for use with existing antiviral therapy to treat chronic hepatitis B in adults without cirrhosis.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that the new biologic expands treatment options for chronic HBV patients without cirrhosis and must incorporate its labeling, dosing, and combination‐therapy considerations into product dossiers and marketing materials.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
entries.description: Today, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week.
entries.summary: The FDA has approved the first generic version of the once‑weekly Climara Pro transdermal hormone therapy patch for women.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should monitor the availability of the generic to update product listings, pricing, and labeling information for patients with an intact uterus.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Allow Certain Patients with Rectal Cancer to Avoid Chemotherapy, Radiation and Surgery
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for a new use of the immunotherapy Jemperli (dostarlimab-gxly) that may allow some patients with locally advanced rectal cancer to avoid common treatments that can have a lasting impact on their daily life.
entries.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Jemperli as a new use in locally advanced rectal cancer to potentially spare patients from chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery.
entries.why_it_matters: This approval expands treatment options for rectal cancer patients and requires RA teams to update labeling, monitor post‑marketing data, and communicate the new indication to stakeholders.

entries.description: It is widely recognised that AI technologies have the potential to positively transform healthcare by improving patient outcomes, supporting clinical decision-making and helping health services work more efficiently. However, AI systems can behave differently once they move from controlled testing …
entries.summary: MHRA prioritises post‑market surveillance for AI systems under the Airlock programme.
